issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` will match identifiers like `dms` or `1s` inside arbitrary strings, not just time tokens.
issues.detail: The fast-path filter is fine as a cheap gate before the real parser runs, since valueParser still does the authoritative work. But the pattern matches things like `transform: translateX(1s)` or a custom-property name containing `1ms`. It's a pre-filter, not a validator, so this is acceptable — just note it in a comment so the next maintainer doesn't think it's a parser.

issues.description: No benchmark numbers in the changeset or PR body.
issues.detail: Claim is "fixed performance." Show me the numbers. Before/after on a representative stylesheet, in the commit message or changeset. Prose about performance without a measurement is the kind of thing that gets silently regressed in six months because nobody knows what the baseline was. One line with timings would settle it.

issues.description: No test demonstrating the hot path is actually skipped.
issues.detail: The change is small and obviously correct by reading, and existing rule tests should still pass. But a unit test asserting that decls without time-shaped values short-circuit before `valueParser` runs would lock in the optimization. Otherwise a future refactor moves the parse back above the guard and nobody notices.

review.summary: Small, well-shaped patch. One file, one purpose: skip the expensive valueParser call when the declaration value obviously can't contain a time. Diff is readable, matches surrounding style, doesn't introduce abstractions, doesn't reach beyond its scope. This is the right shape for a perf fix. The regex is a coarse pre-filter — that's fine and arguably good taste, since the real parsing still runs on candidates — but it deserves a one-line comment saying so, plus actual before/after numbers in the changeset. ACCEPT with nits.
